A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PMF-based LVLM performance-prediction study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 108 LVLMs across 176 datasets, performance-prediction experiments, active evaluation, ablations and appendix generalization results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations involving newer models and benchmarks, alternative predictors, evaluation-setting perturbations, coreset combinations, ranking metrics and computational costs.

M1.justification: The Section 3 PMF/PTF framework remains unchanged. Sections 5.2–5.3 add bounded adaptations: representing evaluation settings through additional model rows or profiles, and combining PMF with coreset predictions through averaging or uncertainty-guided fusion. These change parts of the prediction procedure without replacing its core.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark coverage and adds MathVision, EMMA, Video-MME and LongVideoBench, expanding mathematical/multimodal reasoning and video evaluation, including long-video understanding. Section 5.2 also introduces corrupted-image testing. These extend the represented tasks and input conditions beyond the original matrix.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's mean-based prediction baselines, v2 Table 10 evaluates Deep Matrix Factorization and Graph Convolutional Matrix Completion. Tables 4 and 14 additionally compare Random Selection, Herding and K-Center Greedy coreset predictors and their combinations with PMF. TinyBenchmarks' earlier citation alone did not constitute these comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes the reported active-evaluation design from initially masking 80% of scores to explicit 20% training, 60% acquisition-pool and 20% test partitions. Added protocols include observing 20% or 50% of new matrix blocks, ranking metrics, confidence-based prediction filtering, coreset sampling fractions and controlled prompt/decoding variations. The original NUTS sampling schedule is retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test Gaussian image noise, prompt changes, sampling temperatures and beam search; compare coreset fusion strategies and sampling fractions; and examine retaining only confident predictions. The earlier low-rank, profile, vision-encoder and zero-observation generalization analyses remain present, sometimes relocated to appendices.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 4 displays shaded ranges around its repeated-run curves, whereas v2 Figure 4 omits them. Their precise statistical meaning was not specified in v1. Both versions retain ten-seed averaging for active evaluation and enhancement experiments, and other error-bar displays remain.

E6.justification: v2 adds transfer, robustness, timing, ranking, neural-baseline and coreset results. For example, new Table 10 reports overall RMSE of 0.193 for PMF versus 0.225 for DMF at 20% masking. The original detailed PMF/PTF tables retain their numerical values. Figure 4 supplies replacement results under the revised protocol, while its MAE panel and Table 1's MAE entries are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds explicit top-K hit-rate definitions: Precision@K tests whether the predicted best model belongs to the true top K, while Recall@K tests whether the true best belongs to the predicted top K. The PMF/PTF likelihoods, priors, assumptions and profile equations remain mathematically unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The three central contributions—performance prediction through PMF, uncertainty-based active evaluation and sparse-data enhancements—are retained. v2's introduction additionally claims demonstrated generalization through expanding the matrix to new models and datasets, modestly broadening the stated contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations based on benchmark redundancy, shared architectures/training data, and differences between transfer to new models and new datasets. It interprets coreset and PMF predictions as complementary. The conclusion drops v1's cautions about uninformative high-uncertainty evaluations and identifying needed benchmarks; the existing zero-observation limitation is retained and promoted to the conclusion.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information with DMF/GCMC training configurations, exact prompts and decoding settings, coreset embedding/selection details, A100 timing measurements, additional model checkpoints, and new dataset counts and access links. These largely document added experiments rather than establish changes to existing implementations. The project's code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: Focused additions distinguish the work from Zhang et al. (2024c)'s concurrent LLM performance-prediction study and explicitly position it as complementary to coreset methods. References also expand to neural matrix completion, newer models/benchmarks and benchmark redundancy. The central positioning around PMF for efficient LVLM evaluation remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work prose are revised, and the discussion is reorganized around predictability, varying evaluation settings and coreset integration. The original low-rank discussion moves to Appendix B; the appendices are reorganized into A–C with five experimental subsections. Publication information and an impact statement are also added.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main document to a two-column conference layout, redraws Figure 1, and restructures Figure 4 from three panels into two with different axes. Table 1 drops its MAE columns, numerous experimental tables are added, and existing analyses and figures are redistributed between the main text and appendices. The original heatmaps are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps by explicitly separating acquisition from held-out testing and adding substantive matrix-completion comparisons. Transfer experiments and controlled setting perturbations substantially strengthen evidence about applicability beyond the original matrix. Reporting shortcomings remain: Figure 4 loses shaded ranges, and Table 13 leaves its two result blocks unlabeled. These limited drawbacks do not outweigh the stronger experimental validation.
